answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce token for a fixed period before it may place orders, with larger limits requiring larger locks. The protocol caps rewards per locked token and slashes deposits for provable double-spending or collusion, so splitting capital across identities yields no extra influence while multiplying fees and locked funds. An attacker must acquire real capital and keep it unavailable; names like ivory, wander, or meadow do not bypass that cost.
